figure.name: Donald Trump
figure.era: Brand, real estate, media, and presidential power (1970-present)
figure.role: Real estate businessman, media figure, political leader, and example of capital, brand, debt, law, spectacle, and state power crossing into each other.
figure.hook: Trump = real estate, brand power, media politics, and capital entering government.
whyHere: Trump belongs here because modern capitalism is not only factories or technology. It is real estate, branding, licensing, debt, media attention, inheritance, litigation, and political office.
He matters because his path makes the border between private business, public power, media spectacle, and political loyalty impossible to ignore.
figure.cleanIdea: Capital can become political power when property, brand, media attention, party politics, and state authority reinforce one another. Trump is not on the page as a cartoon villain; he is there because modern capitalism can turn ownership, debt, spectacle, and office into one public-force machine.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: Real estate, inherited capital, brand licensing, television, debt, law, and presidential power become one modern capitalism doorway.

ideas.title: Real Estate Capital
ideas.plainDefinition: Real estate capital is wealth and power built through land, buildings, rent, debt, zoning, development, taxes, speculation, and location.
ideas.context: In the Trump path, real estate is not just buildings. It is inheritance, leverage, city politics, branding, and legal conflict.
ideas.whyMatters: Real estate capital matters because property can become political influence, social status, and public-policy pressure. Buildings sit inside law: zoning, tax treatment, lending, permits, courts, labor, inheritance, and city politics all shape who profits.

sources.title: Business career of Donald Trump / Wikipedia

ideas.title: Brand Politics
ideas.plainDefinition: Brand politics is the use of personal image, media attention, slogans, loyalty, spectacle, and market identity as political force.
ideas.context: In the Trump path, the business brand and political identity reinforce each other.
ideas.whyMatters: Brand politics matters because modern power can be sold, watched, repeated, and defended like a product. This is not only advertising; it is identity, loyalty, media repetition, grievance, celebrity, and the conversion of attention into political force.

ideas.title: Political Capitalism
ideas.plainDefinition: Political capitalism is the study of how private wealth, public office, regulation, contracts, courts, parties, lobbying, and state power interact.
ideas.context: In the Trump path, private business identity and public authority meet directly.
ideas.whyMatters: Political capitalism matters because democracy has to ask when private gain, public office, and state authority become entangled. This room is where conflicts of interest, state power, courts, business networks, and voter loyalty have to be studied together instead of separately.
